observations: Single photo shows a white plastic clothes iron (non-steam/dry type) lying on a tiled floor.
Soleplate (metal pressing plate) is visible, dark-edged, with some dirt/residue around the heel.
Body is dusty/dirty with visible stains and discoloration.
Power cord is a fabric/rubber-covered cord that appears frayed and tangled, with bare/exposed wire strands visible near the point where the cord meets the plug and near the iron body.
A 3-pin plug is attached but the wiring at the plug terminals looks loose/exposed rather than neatly fitted.
No brand name, logo, or model number is visible anywhere on the iron.
No photo shows the iron plugged in, heating, or steam/power indicator lit.

claims.claim: A used dry pressing iron that is still working is available for sale.

risks.risk: Exposed/frayed wiring near plug and cord could mean the iron is unsafe to use or non-functional.
risks.proof: Close-up photo or short video of the cord insulation and plug wiring, ideally showing the plug intact and the cord undamaged along its length.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having a damaged/unsafe cord, i.e., needing cord replacement before use

risks.risk: Claim of 'still working' cannot be confirmed from a static photo.
risks.proof: A short video clip showing the iron plugged in and heating up, or the heat dial/indicator light working.

risks.risk: Soleplate condition (scratches, burn marks, or residue) could affect ironing quality.
risks.proof: A clear, well-lit close-up photo of the soleplate surface.

risks.risk: No brand or model is visible, so build quality and spare-part availability are unknown.
risks.proof: A photo of any brand label or nameplate, often on the handle or base.

proof_requests: Video of the iron plugged in and heating, showing temperature dial movement or indicator light.
Close-up photo of the cord and plug wiring to confirm no exposed bare wires.
Clear photo of the soleplate surface.
Photo of any brand/model label on the iron body or handle.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable by type as a used dry pressing iron, but the 'still working' claim is unverified and the cord shows visible wear/possible exposed wiring, so it must be priced at worst case as a non-working, unsafe-cord unit until proof is given.
